scope_note: Native C compatibility transport is deleted, including raw submission/decoder/batch writer/statistics and ten obsolete wire records. Core adoption and apply_now are deleted; native clone/input use committed state and atomic editor edits publish prepared dependencies. Rust-only submit/submit_indexed, compatibility queue/temp IDs and presentation overrides remain: full transport retirement and F2 are NOT complete.
integration_findings: Native ABI, resource-registration, leak and independent-module identity tests migrated to actual owned C gameplay begin/exchange/end; no queue emulator, temporary-ID map or synthetic spawn event helper was introduced.
All 20 native ABI tests retain subsystem/query/lifecycle coverage and assert immediate all-or-nothing validation instead of the retired per-command/lane policy.
Cooked asset registration regression covers stale-owner rejection, valid resource preparation followed by later failure, no publication/replay, and successful retry.

Native clone/input no longer adopt unrelated queued work. Core adoption regressions now exercise shared transactions, event preservation, unique scoped handles, rollback, resource union/preflight/deduplication and exactly-once effect delivery.
Atomic live editor edits prepare/stage the resource union and publish it only after commit. Per-command apply_now is removed, and preview sun transaction errors propagate to native authoring.

Ten obsolete command/envelope/bus record fixtures were removed from current cross-language test registration; SDK test total decreases from 580 to 570 for that reason. All retained codecs use new fingerprint 0x8da8b43e4b1f1c3e.

Initial full Rust qualification found a schema-layout unit test referencing the removed SpawnCommand; it now checks the retained SceneReadyEvent string layout. An unused legacy asset-test helper was removed. Failed runs remain archived.
Fresh dynamic-library gate passes and checks that both retired C exports are absent while shared identity authority survives independent module replacement.
No claim is made that Rust core submission queues, temporary IDs or legacy presentation overrides are deleted. They are the remaining transport-retirement task.
